- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast peak and add early mean-reversion bias.  
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, model underestimates trend — increase forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment supports it.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 5+ days, apply downward bias correction (e.g., subtract 0.5–1.5% per day) unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome over 5+ days, apply upward bias correction (e.g., add 0.5–1.5% per day) unless sentiment is strongly bearish.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong divergence from 10-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 10-day trend unless sentiment is neutral.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is trending, apply mean-reversion bias toward recent 7-day average unless true outcome shows strong momentum.
